answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition probabilities normalized by edge weights and node influence capped. A Sybil cluster linked to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance; when trust is cut-aware and incoming attestations are bounded, its aggregate voting weight is limited by the cut capacity, not by the number of identities it creates. Labels such as onyx, jetty, and knoll do not change this bound.
